newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks hit fresh closing high on Friday.
newsitem.headline: French stocks hit fresh closing high on Friday.

text.p: French shares hit a fresh closing high on Friday on the back of a continued Wall Street rally and underpinned by a home made run in financial shares.

Friday's gains could have been bigger but for a 10 point index fall just before the close and traders said that there could be further profit-taking next week because the share future was close to resistance at 2.270/72. "In principle, we should be suffering but if we break through the 2,272, nobody knows where we could go," one said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 22.15 points or one percent at 2,240.33. It hit an intra-day high of 2,250.29.
The November future closed 21 points at 2,247.

The market has been moving from high to high at levels last seen in the first quarter of 1994 since Tuesday's announcement by insurers Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) and AXA that they plan to merge through a share swap. The news sparked a rally in financial shares.
Paris had been closed on Monday for Armistice Day.
The blue-chip index gained 1.6 percent this week.
The market's all-time high was at 2,360.98 on February 2, 1994. Volume was a hefty 8.42 billion francs of which 6.34 billion in blue-chip shares.
* UAP closed 1.40 percent lower at 134.10 after a leap on Thursday and AXA closed 1.60 percent down at 301.60. UAP was heaviest traded stock, followed by AXA and Eurotunnel.
* Take-over fever spread to other financial shares and links such as BNP, up 0.76 percent at 211.40, with Paribas, up 5.04 percent at 368.70 francs, were touted.
* Suez added 1.86 percent to 224.10 francs, also helped by hopes of an imminent property asset sale. The holding is seen posting a hefty capital loss but the deal could help curtail property woes.
* Societe Generale was up 1.23 percent at 577.
"The market has been pulled up by the financials and cyclicals but in fact the majority of the CAC-40 has been bought. Foreigners have big buy programmes on financials," a dealer said.
Another added that "the market is starting to play some cyclicals such as Renault, Peugeot or Lafarge because we are at a turning point. People are looking for ideas."

* Renault closed 2.5 percent higher at 123.10 francs despite posting lower overall sales and saying losses at its trucks divison would be bigger than expected. Analysts said that in fact the car division's sales were better than expected.

* LVMH closed 1.34 percent lower at 1,247 francs. It had earlier cancelled deep opening losses on a report U.S. investment bank Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co had approached shareholders of DFS about making a bid. Sources close LVMH, which last month agreed to buy a 58.75 percent stake in DFS for 12.6 billion francs, said the KKR bid was conditional on LVMH withdrawing, which it did not plan.

* L'Oreal closes 3.73 percent higher at 1,863, but below fresh year high of 1,876 with dealers unsure about the exact reason but pointing to heavy weighting of L'Oreal in CAC index and therefore influence of buys in basket trades.
* L'Oreal said it hosted a "classic" investors road show in Geneva today following its sales figures on Tuesday.
* Alcatel closed 1.54 percent higher at 456.10 francs, benefiting from Thursday's third quarter results of Finland's Nokia which showed a big rise in mobile telecommunications.
* Euro Disney, up 3.40 percent at 10.65 francs, will publish full-year results for 1995/96 on Tuesday.
* Pechiney, down 6.13 percent at 196.00 francs, further pummelled for profit warning after analysts meeting.
